To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a substantial proportion of neurons in the MTL persistently respond to images presented in a working memory task; and 2) the persistent activity of these MTL neurons predicts the outcome of a subsequent recognition task.

(1) 48% of visually-selective neurons continued to carry information about previously presented images after image offset; (2) most neurons ceased to encode previously-presented images after a subsequent image presentation, but 8% of neurons encoded previously presented items despite presentation of further items in the intervening interval; (3) population activity of stimuli-selective neurons predicted correct and incorrect behavioral responses.

8% of neurons in the human medial temporal lobe continue to encode previously presented stimuli across a brief delay, and that population activity of stimulus selective neurons predicts behavioral outcome in terms of correct and incorrect responses.
